reasoning_summary: Round 1 uses the baseline assessment only, since there is no prior-round feedback. The baseline indicates underfitting with low train and CV R², so the grid should ensure the model is not overly constrained while remaining appropriate for the dataset size. Here, n_train=153 is moderate, but n_features=1 means PLSRegression capacity is inherently limited: n_components can only be 1 because it must be in 1..min(n_features, n_train-1)=1. Given this single-feature setting, the practical search space is compact and focuses on preprocessing via scale and solver convergence via max_iter.
search_strategy: Compact baseline-focused grid exploring all valid model capacity and preprocessing options under the one-feature constraint.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Low risk of increasing overfitting because model complexity is fixed at one latent component due to the single available feature.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: Limited ability to reduce underfitting because n_components cannot exceed 1; scaling and convergence settings may yield modest gains if preprocessing or optimization was suboptimal.
warnings: With n_features=1, PLSRegression is effectively restricted to n_components=1, so hyperparameter tuning has limited leverage against underfitting.
If performance remains poor after this round, the main bottleneck is likely descriptor informativeness rather than PLS hyperparameters.
